title: Shared Well-Being Is the True Measure of Development, Sheinbaum Says; Her APEC Participation Ends Today
author: Ángeles Cruz Martínez
content:
_This article by[Ángeles Cruz
Martínez](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/%C3%81ngeles%20Cruz%20Mart%C3%ADnez%2C%20enviada),
special correspondent originally appeared in the [November 19, 2026 edition of
La Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/19/economia/sheinbaum-
el-desarrollo-debe-dar-vida-digna-a-los-pueblos-hoy-concluye-su-participacion-
en-la-apec), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Shenzhen.** On the final day of her visit to China, President Claudia
Sheinbaum took part in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’
plenary session, where she warned of the profound inequalities facing humanity
and stressed the importance of technological innovation contributing to
people’s well-being.

She emphasized: “In Mexico, we believe that development should not be measured
solely by economic growth, the size of markets or technological leadership;
efforts must be made to ensure that everyone has a dignified life and that
families have housing, food, employment and education. That is the vision of
Mexico’s government.”

Earlier, the 21 APEC leaders posed for the official photograph with colored
scarves around their necks, 10 blue and 11 red.

Then came addresses by the host, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and
International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva.

Other media outlets broadcast the addresses by US President Donald Trump and
Russian President Vladimir Putin.

![Claudia Sheinbaum and Donald Trump sit facing each other with members of
their delegations.](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/shared-wellbeing-apec-development-
photo-1.webp)President Claudia Sheinbaum said she had a “very good meeting”
yesterday with her US counterpart, Donald Trump, during which they reviewed
progress in bilateral trade negotiations. Photo: Presidency.

When her turn came, Sheinbaum said it was a decisive moment for humanity, in
which technological transformations, including artificial intelligence, are
opening up enormous possibilities. “That is why it is worth asking ourselves
what world we want to build and what kinds of relationships we want to
establish between our economies.”

Thanks to current policies in Mexico, she said, **more than 17 million people
have left poverty**. “That should be the purpose of our economies and the
meaning of our cooperation,” she maintained.

The president insisted on the need for economies to complement one another “to
guarantee **affordability without undermining each one’s productive
capacity**.”

> “True prosperity consists of creating the conditions for all nations to
> grow, develop their capabilities and offer their peoples a better life. The
> development of one country must not be an obstacle for another, but an
> opportunity for all.”

Thus, the logic of some winning and others losing must end, giving way to one
in which “we all win, in which shared prosperity is multiplied.” APEC was born
in that spirit, she said.

Later, she insisted that investing in the development of other nations is
neither a concession nor a loss, but a contribution to **a more stable, just
and prosperous world**.

With that “vision of cooperation for development and shared prosperity, we
will see you in Vietnam, and we welcome you with open arms to the 35th APEC
Leaders’ Forum in our country,” she concluded.

This Thursday, Sheinbaum is scheduled to meet with the IMF managing director,
as well as the prime ministers of Singapore, Lawrence Wong, and Australia,
Anthony Albanese. Afterward, she will hold a press conference and travel back
to Mexico that night on a commercial flight.

On Wednesday night, during the APEC leaders’ dinner, she spoke briefly with
José Antonio Kast, president of Chile, and Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori.
